artifacts.title: Flesher and Weekly v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: In Complaint 2015-03, Steve Flesher and Randy Weekly challenged Metro Atlanta Presbytery, but the SJC did not reach the merits. Because the issues raised had already been adjudicated in Appeal 2015-08, the SJC declared Complaint 2015-03 moot and approved that disposition. The short decision thus records a mootness ruling based on prior appellate adjudication; the underlying presbytery action and the Appeal 2015-08 decision are not described in the supplied text.

artifacts.synopsis: TE John Hardie appealed his Metro Atlanta Presbytery conviction on three charges of breaking ordination vows and indefinite suspension, alleging seventeen procedural and evidentiary errors. Applying BCO 39-2/3 clear-error deference, the SJC denied every specification and upheld the judgment and censure. It found no clear error in the BCO 31-2 investigation, indictment/prosecutor process, commission membership, evidence rulings, scheduling, alleged prejudice, or censure. It assessed transcription costs equally while encouraging MAP to absorb them, and cautioned that an absent commissioner's vote might support a future challenge.

artifacts.title: Spann v. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church
artifacts.synopsis: An individual appealed directly to the SJC, alleging her church effectively excommunicated her without process, failed the Matthew 18 process, and spiritually abused her by social isolation. The SJC dismissed as premature, without reaching the merits, because there was no record of a judicial decision by the church or of an appeal to Evangel Presbytery, the next higher court; it stated she could proceed only by providing such evidence. The severity of excommunication did not excuse that prerequisite. The SJC asked Presbytery to obtain the session's written response to her letter.

artifacts.synopsis: Louisiana Presbytery’s refusal to institute process after examining Steve Wilkins’s Federal Vision teachings was challenged for applying the wrong constitutional standard and overlooking a strong presumption that some views were out of conformity with the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s denial. A “difference” need not expressly contradict the Standards; Presbytery must independently investigate and classify it rather than accept the member’s assurance or shift the burden to objectors. The ruling did not adjudicate Wilkins’s guilt; the Central Carolina memorial remained before the SJC.

artifacts.synopsis: Westminster Presbytery was found to have erred in its BCO 31-2 investigation of secret taping by TE Frank Smith by failing to obtain full witness testimony and investigate legal ramifications; case remanded. The court found no proof of partiality and declined to require establishment of unbiblical criteria for secret taping. Vote: 18 concurring, 1 dissenting (RE Frederick Neikirk), 2 recused, 1 abstained, 2 absent.

artifacts.title: Mt. Carmel Session v. New Jersey Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Mt. Carmel Session challenged New Jersey Presbytery's creation-days resolution, arguing that the Westminster Standards require six consecutive twenty-four-hour days. The SJC majority concluded that Presbytery could resolve the doctrinal question under BCO 11-4 and that prior Assembly actions permitted latitude on the length of the creation days. The General Assembly rejected the minority report, adopted the majority report, and denied the complaint.

artifacts.title: Scope and duration of BCO debate prohibitions during a complaint

matches.evidence: BCO prohibitions on debate apply only to the specific matter complained, only until final adjudication, and to all members of the lower court — expiring upon final resolution.
